comparisonCore.headline: CET compression remains zero-materialization while ASPs stay optional accelerators.

aspBacked.happyPath: ASP batches the selected virtual-CET payout into an Ark round and avoids on-chain CET fanout
aspBacked.challengePath: Shinigami fraud claim plus BitVM reserve challenge slashes bad payout, underdelivery, or withheld exit obligations

directDlcBitvm.happyPath: oracle-selected virtual-CET payout root is accepted and the direct vault spends by cooperative or timeout path
directDlcBitvm.challengePath: BitVM challenge opens the Shinigami public claim if a counterparty proposes the wrong outcome, wrong payout, or omitted virtual-CET leaf
directDlcBitvm.feeTradeoff: removes ASP route and exit-withholding risk, but loses Ark round batching and ASP-funded watcher incentives

threats.aspBacked: Shinigami claim binds selected leaf, payout root, and collateral sum; ASP reserve slash pays users if the ASP advances the wrong payout.
threats.directDlcBitvm: Shinigami claim still detects the wrong payout, but the remedy is a direct BitVM challenge against the vault instead of an ASP reserve claim.
threats.residualRisk: watcher must publish the challenge before timeout

threats.aspBacked: ASP-signed virtual-CET settlement must match the oracle outcome hash or the route becomes slashable.
threats.directDlcBitvm: Counterparty cannot rely on an ASP route, but the direct vault still depends on oracle publication freshness and challenge liveness.
threats.residualRisk: oracle compromise or stale oracle policy remains outside CET compression

threats.aspBacked: Ark leaf root and virtual-CET set id are public inputs; omission is challenged against ASP round state.
threats.directDlcBitvm: Direct vault commits the virtual-CET set root before funding; omission is challenged against the funding template.
threats.residualRisk: large sets still need reproducible corpus generation and archival

threats.aspBacked: ASP can misroute, but the reserve bond and forfeit path make it economically slashable.
threats.directDlcBitvm: No ASP route exists, so this class disappears; users pay with slower direct coordination.
threats.residualRisk: direct model inherits counterparty noncooperation risk

threats.aspBacked: Exit availability is an ASP-signed obligation with reserve slash and watcher bounty.
threats.directDlcBitvm: No ASP can withhold an Ark exit, but the direct vault must have timeout/refund leaves and both parties must preserve transaction packages.
threats.residualRisk: timeout design and fee bumping need production hardening

threats.aspBacked: ASP can batch and patch liquidity cheaply; underdelivery is measurable against signed obligations.
threats.directDlcBitvm: No liquidity provider liveness assumption, but no cheap batched liquidity service either.
threats.residualRisk: ASP market concentration and reserve sizing

threats.aspBacked: Watcher bounty funds third-party monitoring, and reserve claims define public receipts.
threats.directDlcBitvm: Participants or their watchtowers must monitor directly; no ASP reserve subsidizes monitoring by default.
threats.residualRisk: watcher availability and mempool fee spikes
